terms.gloss: a thing that happens, an event, an affair
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.13.2: rēs dignae litterīs nostrīs
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: a matter, affair, event, fact, occurrence. What happened is also said with a clause, quod accidit, quid reliquīs acciderit (Caes. BC 1.21). For an organised event Latin names the occasion: convīvium, spectāculum, lūdī.

terms.latin: rēs gestae, rērum gestārum f. pl.
terms.grammar: noun, fifth declension, plural, with a participle

terms.gloss: a chance event, an accident, a misfortune
evidence: Cic. Div. 2.15: quid cāsus, quid ēventus (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: an occurrence; far more often, the outcome
evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.63: cōnsilia prīmum, deinde ācta, posteā ēventūs exspectantur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Rare in the sense of an event; usually the result of an action (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: sunt autem post discessum ā mē tuum rēs dignae litterīs nostrīs
phrases.english: since you left me there have been events worth a letter

sources: Lewis & Short: res · Lewis & Short: gero · Lewis & Short: casus · Lewis & Short: eventus
